metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.topic: Waves — Definition of a Longitudinal Wave
metadata.note: 3-token DDWTOS completing: 'A longitudinal wave is one in which the [vibration] of the particles is [parallel] to the [direction of travel] of the wave.' 3 tokens; marks 0.5+1.0+0.5=2m. The key discriminator is 'parallel' (not perpendicular, which describes transverse waves). Distractors: perpendicular/transverse/amplitude.

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q5a — Define Longitudinal Wave
question.text:
Define the term 'longitudinal wave' by completing the statement below:

A longitudinal wave is one in which the [[1]] of the particles is [[2]] to the [[3]] of the wave.
question.general_feedback:
Definition: A longitudinal wave is one in which the vibration of the particles is parallel to the direction of travel of the wave.

Examples of longitudinal waves: Sound waves, compression waves in a spring (slinky)

Compare with transverse waves: In a transverse wave, the vibration is perpendicular to the direction of travel (e.g. light waves, water surface waves).

Key distinction: Longitudinal → parallel | Transverse → perpendicular

ddwtos.cloze_html: A longitudinal wave is one in which the [[1]] of the particles is [[2]] to the [[3]] of the wave.

groups.label: Longitudinal wave — ___ of particles is...
groups.diagnostic_hint: The VIBRATION (oscillation) of particles is in a specific direction — parallel to wave travel. The motion of particles, not the wave itself, is what this blank describes.

groups.label: Longitudinal wave — vibration is ___ to direction of travel
groups.diagnostic_hint: Vibration is PARALLEL to the direction of travel. This distinguishes longitudinal waves (sound, P-waves) from transverse waves (light, S-waves) where vibration is perpendicular.

groups.label: Longitudinal wave — parallel to the ___
groups.diagnostic_hint: Parallel to the DIRECTION OF TRAVEL (or direction of propagation). In a sound wave, air molecules vibrate back-and-forth in the same direction the wave is moving.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 11 tokens for 3 slots. 'parallel' (1m) is the critical term — swapping with 'perpendicular' would make the definition describe a TRANSVERSE wave. 'amplitude' distractor in slot 1: students may confuse properties of wave with the particle motion. 'transverse' distractor in slot 2: students who know the wave TYPE may insert the TYPE name rather than the geometric relationship. Both 'vibration' and 'oscillation' are accepted in slot 1; both 'direction of travel' and 'direction of propagation' are accepted in slot 3.
